corpus_meta.purpose: Golden corpus of category-resolution test cases for the replay harness (scripts/replay-corpus.mjs). Each case captures an item description plus the category outcome the resolver MUST produce against the frozen taxonomy snapshot in corpus/ebay_taxonomy_snapshot.json. Run after any change to category-lookup, leafCategoryGuard, suggestedCategories, or the analyze-item AI prompt's category allowlist.
sources: category_mappings_rows.csv (40 rows, exported 2026-08-23) -- every row audited against the taxonomy snapshot
CATEGORY_RESOLVER_V2_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md Finding B (6 dead World Coin IDs) and the PR #529 fix (category 99/256 non-leaf rollups)
The 1893 Columbian Half Dollar live incident

case_kinds.must_resolve: Resolver must land on expected_category_id (a confirmed live leaf) and must NOT return any id in forbidden_category_ids.
case_kinds.must_not_regress: A previously-broken hardcoded ID must remain absent from any allowlist/candidate the resolver could surface; expected_category_id is the confirmed-live replacement.
case_kinds.must_confirm: No candidate should be auto-shipped; the resolver must return needsConfirmation=true / found=false instead of guessing.
case_kinds.quarantine_needs_review: Existing ai_auto mapping in category_mappings that is leaf-valid but is either mislabeled, imprecise, or a duplicate of a verified generic mapping -- not a hard resolver bug, tracked so Phase 5's hygiene-cron rewrite has a concrete list to act on.

forbidden_id_fields.forbidden_category_ids: Ids that must NEVER be shippable for ANY item, because they are dead/non-leaf/rollup nodes in the live taxonomy tree. The replay harness verifies these are absent-or-non-leaf in the snapshot AND (for must_not_regress cases) present in leafCategoryGuard.ts's KNOWN_PARENT_CATEGORY_IDS.
forbidden_id_fields.forbidden_wrong_answer_ids: Ids that ARE valid live leaves elsewhere in the tree, but would be the WRONG answer for this specific item (a plausible mis-identification, not a dead id). The replay harness only checks these are real leaves (so the corpus case itself is well-formed) -- it does NOT expect them to be blocklisted, since blocking a real leaf globally would break legitimate listings that actually belong there.

cases.description: Synthetic worst case: if every real candidate genuinely fails leaf verification (e.g. eBay API degraded, DB has no exact match), the resolver must surface NEEDS_CONFIRMATION rather than shipping category 99 or any other guess

cases.description: category_mappings has two user_verified, approved mappings ('silver jewelry', 'gold jewelry') pinned to 10986, whose own stored breadcrumb 'Fine Jewelry > Necklaces & Pendants' is a plausible-looking but non-existent category id in the live tree
cases.expected_breadcrumb: Jewelry & Watches > Fine Jewelry > Necklaces & Pendants
cases.notes: NEW finding from the Phase 3 corpus audit. This is the most subtle case in the corpus: the stored breadcrumb text ('Fine Jewelry > Necklaces & Pendants') is CORRECT, but the numeric id (10986) it's paired with is not the live id for that breadcrumb -- the live id is 261993. This proves breadcrumb text alone cannot be trusted to validate an id; the id itself must be checked against the taxonomy snapshot. eBay's tree also has 5 other 'Necklaces & Pendants' leaves under different parents (Fashion Jewelry=155101, Men's Jewelry=137839, Handcrafted & Artisan=110655, Children's=84607, Vintage & Antique=262013, Ethnic/Regional/Tribal=261984) -- picking the right one requires the jewelry sub-type, not just the leaf name, which is a Phase 4 concern (aspect/attribute-based disambiguation), not a Phase 3 corpus concern.

cases.description: category_mappings has two mappings for American Silver Eagle (one user_verified, one ai_auto, both with a recorded successful publish) pinned to 41111, which is absent from the current live tree
cases.expected_breadcrumb: Coins & Paper Money > Bullion > Silver > Coins
cases.notes: NEW finding from the Phase 3 corpus audit. Unlike the other non-coin non-leaf cases, this one HAS a recorded publish_success_count=1 on both rows (dated 2026-08-11), meaning 41111 worked at some point and has since been retired/merged by eBay -- a live example of taxonomy drift silently breaking a previously-good mapping. Confirmed replacement via eBay's own current site navigation (searches for 'American Eagle Silver' resolve to category 177653, 'Bullion > Silver > Coins', which is already a leaf in this repo's cache).

cases.description: Two ai_auto quarantine rows ('1989 donruss baseball value', '1992 upper deck scoring') are stored with category_name='Basketball Cards' despite both item_type strings explicitly saying baseball/scoring (Donruss and Upper Deck are historically baseball-card-first brands)
cases.actual_breadcrumb: Sports Mem, Cards & Fan Shop > Sports Trading Cards > Trading Card Singles
cases.notes: The numeric id (261328) IS a valid leaf, so this is not a resolver-correctness bug -- it's a bad cached category_name string that would mislead a human reviewer glancing at the mappings table. Tracked here so Phase 5's category-hygiene-cron rewrite can refresh stale category_name/breadcrumb text from the taxonomy snapshot instead of trusting whatever name was recorded at write time.

cases.description: Row for '1987 1989 donruss baseball' stores category_name literally as the placeholder string 'Category #183437', meaning the code that wrote it never resolved a real name
cases.actual_breadcrumb: Sports Mem, Cards & Fan Shop > Sports Trading Cards > Storage & Display Supplies > Card Sleeves & Bags
cases.notes: 183437 is a valid leaf but describes card SLEEVES/supplies, not the trading cards themselves -- so even though it passes the leaf check, it is very likely the wrong category for a listing described as a baseball card. Flagged for Phase 5 hygiene-cron review, not a hard resolver bug for Phase 3/4 purposes since the corpus's job here is leaf-existence regression, not semantic-fit scoring.

cases.description: 17 of 40 category_mappings rows are year-locked duplicates of a concept that already has a generic, verified row (e.g. '1921 morgan silver dollar' alongside the already-user_verified 'morgan dollar'; three separate Eisenhower Dollar year variants alongside the generic 'eisenhower dollar')
cases.notes: Not a correctness bug (the category ids agree with their generic counterpart in every case checked), but it inflates category_mappings with redundant rows that a token-overlap/exact-match lookup will never actually need, and doubles the blast radius when an id like 41111 goes dead (both the generic and every year-locked variant need fixing). Tracked for Phase 5 hygiene-cron dedup-by-precedence.
